description: After graduating in history he worked as a research assistant at KU Leuven, contributing to the Nieuwe Encyclopedie van de Vlaamse Beweging (New Encyclopedia of the Flemish Movement), and began a doctoral thesis on post-war Flemish-nationalist party formation, which he abandoned in 2002 to devote himself to politics.

First elected office, for the Volksunie, after standing unsuccessfully on the CVP–VU cartel list 'Antwerpen 94' in the 1994 Antwerp municipal election. From January 2000 he also sat on the Volksunie party executive.

role: Co-founder, party executive member, then vice-chairman
description: A member of the 'Oranjehof' group around Geert Bourgeois that opposed the Volksunie's progressive course, he was among the founders of the N-VA after the Volksunie split in 2001, wrote the programme adopted at its first congress in March 2002 and became vice-chairman in October 2003.

Acting chairman from June 2004 after Geert Bourgeois joined the Flemish government, then elected in October 2004 as sole candidate with 95% of the votes and re-elected repeatedly (most recently in November 2020 with 96.8%). He ended the electoral cartel with CD&V in 2008 and led the N-VA to first place in Flanders from 2010 on. He stepped down on becoming Prime Minister after almost 21 years; Valerie Van Peel succeeded him in April 2025 after an interim by Steven Vandeput.

role: Member of the Flemish Parliament (Antwerp constituency)
description: Elected on the CD&V–N-VA cartel list in June 2004; chaired the separate N-VA group from July to November 2004. Left the Flemish Parliament after his election to the Chamber in June 2007.
Sole N-VA councillor elected on the CD&V–N-VA list in 2006; re-elected in 2012, 2018 and 2024.

role: Member of the Chamber of Representatives (Antwerp constituency)
description: Elected second on the CD&V–N-VA list in Antwerp; vice-chairman of the Chamber in 2007–2008. Took part in the long 2007 federal government negotiations, in which N-VA made its support conditional on a state reform, and withdrew that support in September 2008.

role: Member of the Flemish Parliament (Antwerp constituency)
description: Returned to the Flemish Parliament after leading the N-VA list in Antwerp in June 2009; N-VA then joined the Flemish government of Kris Peeters while he stayed party chairman.

role: Community senator (designated by the Flemish Parliament)
description: Elected directly to the Senate in June 2010 with 785,776 preference votes but did not take up that seat; sat instead as a community senator designated by the Flemish Parliament. In 2010 he was royal informateur and then 'clarifier' (verduidelijker) in the 541-day government formation; N-VA left the talks in July 2011 and went into opposition to the Di Rupo government.
Wrote opinion columns setting out his conservative and Flemish-nationalist views, collected in the books Het kostbare weefsel (2008) and Werkbare waarden (2011).

Became mayor after the N-VA won 37.7% of the vote in the October 2012 municipal election, ending decades of socialist-led city government; governed with CD&V and Open Vld (2013–2018), then with Open Vld and sp.a (from 2019) and, after the 2024 election, with Vooruit. Re-sworn on 20 January 2025 for a third term, he handed the exercise of the office to Koen Kennis (interim) and then Els van Doesburg (acting mayor from 24 February 2025) when he became Prime Minister, and remains titular mayor.

role: Member of the Chamber of Representatives (Antwerp constituency)
description: Elected at the head of the N-VA list in Antwerp in May 2014 while remaining mayor and party chairman. He was royal informateur from 27 May to 25 June 2014; the N-VA then joined the 'Swedish' coalition (N-VA, MR, CD&V, Open Vld) led by Charles Michel, in which he took no post; the N-VA left that government in December 2018 over the UN migration pact.

role: Member of the Flemish Parliament (Antwerp constituency)
description: Led the N-VA list in Antwerp province with the stated aim of becoming Flemish Minister-President; after the election he conducted the Flemish formation as informateur, then left the negotiations and the Minister-Presidency to Jan Jambon. In 2020 he and PS chairman Paul Magnette were joint pre-formateurs of a federal government, without success.

role: Member of the Chamber of Representatives (Antwerp constituency)
description: Elected at the head of the N-VA list in Antwerp in June 2024 with 255,446 preference votes; left the Chamber on becoming Prime Minister.

organization: Federal government formation (appointed by King Philippe)
description: Appointed informateur on 12 June 2024, pre-formateur on 26 June and formateur on 10 July 2024. He offered his resignation as formateur on 22 August 2024 after talks stalled; after mediation by Maxime Prévot he resumed the role on 2 September 2024. The five parties reached a coalition agreement on 31 January 2025, 239 days after the elections.

organization: Federal Government of Belgium (De Wever government)
description: Sworn in by King Philippe on 3 February 2025 as head of a five-party coalition of N-VA, MR, Les Engagés, Vooruit and CD&V with 15 ministers and no state secretaries, the first federal government since 2008 with a majority in both language groups. Its main measures include the time limit on unemployment benefits, a pension reform, a capital gains tax, an income-tax reform, the repeal of the nuclear phase-out law, stricter migration rules and a defence increase to 2% of GDP. As of 22 October 2026 the government holds full powers but has not yet agreed its 2027–2029 budget.
